newsitem.title: UK: Coats sees similar H2 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Coats sees similar H2 operating profit.

text.p: UK textiles group Coats Viyella Plc said on Tuesday it expected second-half operating profit to be similar to the second half of 1995.

Coats Viyella repeated pre-tax profits would be hit in the second half by a 55 million stg restructuring programme. Of the total charges, 17.2 million stg were already taken against first-half earnings.
Coats said in September it expected an increase in second-half results year-on-year before the charges.
The group said on Tuesday that trading conditions had remained mixed after a subdued first half.
North America continued its strong recovery in the thread divisions, but the picture was mixed in Europe.
Southern and eastern Europe enjoyed favourable trading, but conditions remained difficult in Northern and Central Europe.
Outside Europe, Coats experienced difficult trading conditions in Brazil and Turkey, where demand was hit by macro-economic problems.
With the exception of the Philippines, the Far East thread markets witnessed continued growth, Coats Viyella said.

In precision engineering, results were hit by general weakness in computer electronics in the Asia/Pacific region and economic uncertainty in Brazil. North American diecasting operations showed a variable performance, while the North American and European plastics businesses were more stable.
High street trading in Britain showed some improvement compared with a year ago. The marked recovery in home furnishings continued, but UK clothing remained mixed.
Fashion retail and the Indian garment business continued to make progress, but the Russian clothing operation suffered from increased competition, Coats Viyella said.
"Market conditions are forecast to remain challenging in 1997, but underlying trading performance is on average expected to show some improvement over 1996," said Coats.
Coats shares were up three pence to 125 at 1500 gmt.
